User.title: User
User.description: Stores user profile information for the NEU Library Check-in app, including authentication details, role, and blockage status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity (Firebase Authentication UID).

email.description: User's institutional email address, strictly restricted to @neu.edu.ph domain.

displayName.description: User's full name or preferred display name.

role.description: User's role in the system. Accepted values are 'admin' or 'user'.

collegeId.description: Reference to the College entity the user belongs to. (Relationship: College 1:N User)

isBlocked.description: Indicates if the user is blocked from accessing the application. True means access is denied.

Visit.title: Visit
Visit.description: Records individual entry logs for library visitors, including who visited, when, and their purpose.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Visit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User entity who made the visit. (Relationship: User 1:N Visit)

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the visit was recorded.

purposeOfVisit.description: The specific reason for the user's visit to the library.

collegeId.description: Reference to the College entity the visitor belongs to at the time of visit. (Relationship: College 1:N Visit)

College.title: College
College.description: Maintains a list of valid colleges, used for dropdown menus and filtering purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the College entity.

name.description: The official name of the college.

definition.description: Dedicated collection for explicit admin role-based access control. The document ID `{userId}` marks a user as an administrator. Used for robust, authorization-independent permission checks (e.g., via 'exists()' in rules).

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication UID of the admin user.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security Rules (QAPs), ensuring clarity, scalability, and debuggability. 

1.  **Users Collection (`/users/{userId}`):** This top-level collection stores individual user profiles. The `userId` matches the Firebase Authentication UID, establishing clear path-based ownership. Each user document contains `role` (admin/user) and `isBlocked` status directly. 
    *   **Authorization Independence:** While `role` and `isBlocked` are crucial for authorization, they reside within the user's own document, which is the primary data source. For global admin checks, an additional `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection is introduced. This separates the explicit `admin` role definition for rules from the `role` field within the user's profile which might be used for UI or other application logic, eliminating `get()` calls to a user's profile for admin status checks in rules. Users can read/update their own profile, while admins can read all profiles and manage `isBlocked` status. 
    *   **QAPs:** Admins can efficiently `list` all users for management and search without needing client-side filtering, as all documents within `/users` share the same read/write permissions for admins. Users can only `get` their own specific document, which is a QAP-friendly operation. 

2.  **Visits Collection (`/visits/{visitId}`):** This collection stores all library visit logs. Each `Visit` document includes `userId` and `collegeId` directly within its own fields. 
    *   **Authorization Independence:** The `userId` field is denormalized into every `Visit` document. This is critical for authorization independence, allowing security rules to verify `request.auth.uid == request.resource.data.userId` for creation without any `get()` operations. This makes rule evaluation atomic and straightforward. `collegeId` is also denormalized to facilitate admin analytics and grouping without cross-collection lookups in rules. 
    *   **QAPs:** Regular users are only permitted to *create* their own visit logs; they cannot `list` other visits or even their own from this collection, as per the strict requirement "Users can only create their own visit logs." Admins, however, are explicitly allowed to `list` all visits. Because all documents in `/visits` have the same security posture for admin reads, admins can perform efficient collection-group queries or direct `list` operations across all visits for analytics without rule violations. 

3.  **Colleges Collection (`/colleges/{collegeId}`):** This collection serves as a master list of colleges. 
    *   **Authorization Independence:** This collection does not rely on parent data for authorization. Its access is defined independently. 
    *   **QAPs:** All authenticated users are permitted to `list` all `College` documents for dropdown menus. This is highly QAP-friendly as all documents have uniform read permissions for authenticated users, allowing efficient retrieval of the entire list. Only admins can modify this collection.

4.  **Admin Roles Collection (`/roles_admin/{userId}`):** This is a dedicated collection to explicitly mark admin users. 
    *   **Authorization Independence:** This collection is the cornerstone for DBAC. A simple `exists()` check against `/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)` determines if the requesting user is an admin. This completely decouples admin role verification from the main `/users` collection, preventing `get()` calls and ensuring atomic rule evaluation and simplified debugging. The documents here are simple markers, potentially just containing the `userId` as the document ID.
    *   **QAPs:** Rules check for the *existence* of a document, not its content or a list. This supports highly efficient authorization checks without requiring `list` operations.
